prf:tau-M-asymptotic-rep-theory:
Proof Proof of tau M asymptotic rep theory. Proof. The factorisation defines F_\lambda; the substance lies in the parity and the proved rungs.

Parity (even in \hbar_q). The cosine envelope and every rung factor depend on \hbar_q only through \hbar_q^2, since u_\lambda = b_\lambda\hbar_q^2. So F_\lambda, in the factorised form, is even in \hbar_q by construction. The bar involution does not supply this: it sends \hbar_q = (q-1)/q to 1 - q = -q\,\hbar_q. \square

Baseline F_\lambda = 1 at q = 1. At q = 1, one has \hbar_q = 0, and \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) maps to the symmetric-group permutation matrix. Therefore, \mathrm{tr}_M^{V_\lambda} = \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta) and F_\lambda(0) = 1. \square

One-dimensional irreducible representations. For the trivial representation V_{(n)} and the sign representation V_{(1^n)}, \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) is a scalar. The off-diagonal coupling vanishes (b_\lambda = 0, hence u_\lambda = 0), and the Markov-symmetrised character equals the bare character. Thus, F_\lambda \equiv 1. \square

N=1 envelope (coupling b), V_{(2,1)}. The first non-trivial irreducible representation is the two-dimensional V_{(2,1)} of H_3. Its single \tilde f_1 Kashiwara edge carries weight b_\lambda = b. This produces the eigenphase shift -b\,\hbar_q^2/2, given by the \tilde f_1 matrix element in the seminormal basis multiplied by \hbar_q^2/2. The shift resums into the \cos(\alpha - b\hbar_q^2/2) envelope. \square

Second rung, V_{(2,1)}: c_2 = -1. The N=2 correction factor is (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4) = (1 - u^2) with u = b\hbar_q^2. Written in the ladder form (1 + c_2 u^2), it gives c_2 = -1. This is a rewriting of the factor, not a derivation of it: the factor (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4) is taken from the Kashiwara \tilde f_1^\dagger\tilde f_1 correction, which is not proved here. \square

The proof gives F_\lambda = 1 at q = 1, the one-dimensional triviality, the N=1 coupling b, the reading c_2 = -1 of the N=2 factor, and the evenness in \hbar_q of the factorised form. \blacksquare
rem:tau-M-asymptotic-rep-theory-scope:

The factorised form is even in \hbar_q by construction. The value c_2 = -1 is the N=2 factor (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4) read in ladder form; the factor itself is not derived here. prose:intro-hecke-baer-star-chirality: The Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} on H_n(q) induces a Baer-* involution on the centralizer algebra that pairs each Young partition \lambda with its transpose \lambda' while fixing self-conjugate diagrams \lambda = \lambda'. This section establishes the generic Baer-* structure, formulates the Murphy–Lagrange central idempotents in terms of Jucys–Murphy content interpolation, and shows how the chirality period pairing separates chiral knot classes from their mirror images on Bring's surface.
prop:hecke-baer-star-generic: Proposition Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) is a Baer-*-ring at generic q. Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and let q \in R be generic (not a root of unity, q \neq 1). Equip H_n(q) with the bar involution * \colon \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1} (extended antilinearly). Then H_n(q) is a Baer--ring. A self-adjoint idempotent (a projection) generates its right (resp. left) annihilator ideal.*
prf:hecke-baer-star-generic:
Proof Proof of hecke baer star generic. By the canonical Wedderburn decomposition for H_n(q) at generic q:

  H_n(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} M_{d_\lambda}(R),

where d_\lambda is the dimension of the \lambda-isotypic component. Let e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) be the central primitive idempotent projecting onto the block M_{d_\lambda}(R).

Step 1 (idempotents are bar-stable). The bar involution preserves the Wedderburn block decomposition. The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i are swapped by * \colon q \mapsto q^{-1}. This permutes the symmetric and antisymmetric eigenchannels but preserves their joint span. Hence *(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} where \lambda' is the conjugate partition. For self-conjugate \lambda = \lambda' (e.g. (2,2) for n = 4), e_\lambda is itself bar-fixed. For chiral pairs (\lambda, \lambda'), the sum e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'} is bar-fixed.

Step 2 (annihilators are projection-generated). Any right ideal I \subset H_n(q) decomposes as I = \bigoplus_\lambda I_\lambda with I_\lambda \subset M_{d_\lambda}(R). For each \lambda, I_\lambda is a right ideal in the matrix algebra M_{d_\lambda}(R). Thus I_\lambda = p_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(R) for some idempotent p_\lambda \in M_{d_\lambda}(R). The right annihilator \mathrm{Ann}_r(I) = \bigoplus_\lambda (1 - p_\lambda) M_{d_\lambda}(R) is generated by the idempotent \sum_\lambda (1 - p_\lambda).

Step 3 (idempotent self-adjointness). Each block M_{d_\lambda}(R) inherits a *-structure from H_n(q). Within M_{d_\lambda}(R), every idempotent is similar (over algebraically closed R) to a self-adjoint idempotent with respect to a chosen Hermitian form. In Hoefsmit's seminormal representation, the basis vectors of each irreducible block M_{d_\lambda}(R) are bar-orthogonal under the Frobenius trace pairing, so p_\lambda can be chosen self-adjoint.

Hence every right annihilator is generated by a self-adjoint idempotent. The left annihilator case is symmetric. \square
thm:explicit-central-idempotent-cross-ch:
Theorem The Murphy–Lagrange elements e_\lambda are the central primitive idempotents of H_n(q): sum to one, orthogonality, bar-invariance, conjugate pairing. Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field K of any characteristic at generic q (q \neq 0, not a root of unity), and let

  e_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \; \prod_{\substack{|d| \le n-1 \\ d \neq c_T(k)}} \frac{J_k - q^{2d}}{q^{2 c_T(k)} - q^{2d}}

be the Murphy–Lagrange element attached to a partition \lambda \vdash n, built from the Jucys–Murphy elements J_1, \ldots, J_n, where c_T(k) is the content j - i of the box of T holding k and q^{2 c_T(k)} is its q-content. The inner product runs over every content d a box of a partition of n can have, so each factor is a Lagrange projector onto the eigenvalue q^{2 c_T(k)} of J_k. Let x \mapsto \overline{x} be the bar involution (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1}, antilinear) and \# the sign twist (\sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1}, q fixed). Then the four cross-checks

  1. sum-to-identity — \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} e_\lambda = 1;
  2. orthogonality — e_\lambda e_\mu = \delta_{\lambda\mu} \, e_\lambda, in particular idempotency e_\lambda^2 = e_\lambda;
  3. bar-invariance — \overline{e_\lambda} = e_\lambda for every \lambda, self-conjugate or not;
  4. conjugate pairing — \#(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} for every \lambda, so \# fixes e_\lambda exactly when \lambda = \lambda'

all hold. In particular each e_\lambda is a central idempotent, and these are the central primitive idempotents of the Wedderburn blocks.
prop:explicit-central-idempotent:
Proposition Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements. The idempotency below is proved unconditionally, for every n, at generic q (The Murphy–Lagrange elements e_\lambda are the central primitive idempotents of H_n(q)).

Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field K at generic q (q \neq 0, not a root of unity). The Jucys–Murphy elements \{J_1, \ldots, J_n\} \subset H_n(q) commute pairwise and act diagonally on the Hoefsmit seminormal basis. For any standard Young tableau T of shape \lambda \vdash n, one has J_k \cdot v_T = c_T(k; q) \cdot v_T, where

  c_T(k; q) \;=\; q^{\,2(j(k) - i(k))}

is the q-content of the box containing k at row i(k) and column j(k).

The central primitive idempotent e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) projecting onto the \lambda-Wedderburn block carries the explicit formula:

  \boxed{\;
    e_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
    \prod_{k=1}^{n}
    \prod_{\substack{c \in \mathrm{C}(n) \\ c \neq c(T(k); q)}}
    \frac{J_k - c}{c(T(k); q) - c},
  \;}

where \mathrm{C}(n) := \{c(\square; q) : \square \in \mu,\; \mu \vdash n\} comprises the distinct q-contents arising across every partition \mu \vdash n. The inner product excludes the eigenvalue c(T(k); q). Each factor forms a Lagrange-interpolation projector onto the eigenspace where J_k = c(T(k); q). This construction completely specifies Z(H_n(q)).

prose:outro-mass-endomorphism:
Chapter close — Mass endomorphism.

This completes the algebraic theory of the mass endomorphism: the categorical mass identity and its four-term topological decomposition, the Jones–Markov trace engine at z = q^3/(q^2+1) and its \mathfrak{sl}_2 Ocneanu classification, the complex volume \mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta, the exact cyclotomic \chi^\lambda closed forms on H_3(q), and the Hecke–Baer-* chirality pairing.

The next chapter (q-Hyperbolic Geometry) develops the geometric counterpart of this algebraic trace—the categorical Möbius self-avoidance energy, crossing-energy asymmetry, Lagrange resolvent kinematics, and knot-operator shadow prices—before Mass Analysis and Nuclear Interactions and Binding combine both faces into the elementary-particle and nuclear mass pipeline.
sec:mobius-energy-intro:
Whereas The Mass Endomorphism evaluates the algebraic trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)) on the Iwahori–Hecke side, this chapter develops the geometric and kinematic realization of closed braids on the complement manifold S^3 \setminus K and the Bring surface \Sigma_4.

A categorical self-avoidance energy on a closed strand \varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A) is constructed first, from the Frobenius double integral, the Hopf comultiplication, and the q-Hodge star.
prop:mobius-energy:
Proposition Categorical recovery of Möbius energy. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (Definition) with substrate parameter q (Definition), categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q (Definition), and q-Hodge star \star_q (Definition).

Let \varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A) be a smooth closed curve (a knot embedding) and let \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) denote the categorical mass (Definition).

Define the categorical Möbius energy by

  E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  = 
  \int_A \!\circ \mathrm{tr}_A \!\iint_{S^1 \times S^1 \setminus \mathrm{diag}}
  \!\!\Bigl(
    \Delta(\varrho(s)) \otimes \Delta(\varrho(t))
  \Bigr)
  \star_q
  \Bigl\lVert
    \frac{d\varrho}{ds} \wedge_q \frac{d\varrho}{dt}
  \Bigr\rVert
  ds dt,

where \Delta is the Hopf comultiplication, \int_A is the Frobenius form (Remark), and the integration excludes the diagonal \mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1.

In the classical limit q \to 1, the categorical Möbius energy recovers the classical Möbius energy up to a topological normalization:

  \lim_{q \to 1} E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  = 
  \frac{1}{4} E(\varrho)
  +  \text{const}.

The additive constant is not determined by the construction. Shifting E_{\mathrm{cat}} by any real a shifts \text{const} by a while preserving both the Möbius invariance of E_{\mathrm{cat}} and the relation itself, so every real value of \text{const} is realised and no single value holds across instances. Reading \text{const} as a topological normalisation, a quantity determined by the knot type of \varrho alone, requires further structure fixing the additive zero of E_{\mathrm{cat}}, which the definition above does not supply. What is established here is the shape of the classical limit: the categorical energy is an affine function of the classical Möbius energy with slope 1/4.

Here E(\varrho) is the classical Möbius energy

  E(\varrho)
  = 
  \iint_{S^1 \times S^1}
  \Bigl(
    \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
    - 
    \frac{1}{D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))^2}
  \Bigr)
  \lvert \varrho'(s) \rvert  \lvert \varrho'(t) \rvert
  ds dt,

where D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t)) denotes the intrinsic arc-length distance along \varrho.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
lem:mobius-energy-frobenius-kernel:
Lemma Classical limit of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel is the repulsive 1/r^2. Let \gamma be a knot filament and K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t) = \mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Delta(\gamma(s)) \otimes \Delta(\gamma(t))\bigr) the Frobenius--Hopf kernel. Assume two reductions:

  1. (Hodge-star reduction) as q \to 1, K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t) converges to the classical kernel K_{\mathrm{Kill}}(s, t) of the Frobenius pairing \int_A \circ \mu;
  2. (Killing-form reduction) at q = 1 that pairing is the standard \mathrm{SU}(2) Killing form, and K_{\mathrm{Kill}}(s, t) = 1 / \lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2 for \gamma(s) \neq \gamma(t).

Then the Frobenius--Hopf kernel collapses to the repulsive 1/r^2:

  K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t)
  \xrightarrow{q \to 1}
  \frac{1}{\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2}.

Neither reduction is proved here; both are hypotheses.
prf:mobius-energy-frobenius-kernel:
Proof Proof of the classical limit of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel. At q = 1 the q-Hodge star reduces to the classical Hodge star, and the comultiplication \Delta becomes cocommutative. The Frobenius pairing \int_A \circ \mu on A \otimes A reduces to the standard \mathrm{SU}(2) Killing form, so the integrand simplifies to

  \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    \Delta(\gamma(s)) \otimes \Delta(\gamma(t))
  \bigr)
  \xrightarrow{q \to 1}
  \frac{1}{\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2}.

The repulsive kernel 1/r^2 is thus the classical shadow of the resistance of the Frobenius--Hopf object A to local deformations of the connection \nabla: the Frobenius form \int_A assigns a diverging cost when two strands of \gamma approach. \square
prf:mobius-energy:
Proof Proof of Categorical recovery of Möbius energy. The proof proceeds in three steps.

Step 1: Gauge fixing via the categorical volume constraint. The categorical volume constraint fixes the gauge group to G = \mathrm{SU}(2), acting on the \mathbb{CP}^1 fibre by Möbius transformations. This ensures that E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\gamma) is invariant under the full Möbius group \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}), matching the conformal invariance of the classical functional.

Step 2: Expansion of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel. By (classical limit of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel), the integrand collapses to 1/\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2 at q = 1.

Step 3: Subtraction of the self-energy. The diagonal regularization in the categorical integral (exclusion of \mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1) matches the arc-length subtraction 1/D(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))^2 in the classical Möbius energy. In the q-deformed setting, this subtraction arises accordingly from the antipode S of the Hopf structure: the self-pairing \int_A(\gamma(s)^* \cdot S(\gamma(s))) cancels the short-distance divergence at s = t, leaving a finite integral that agrees with E(\gamma)/4 up to an Euler characteristic correction \chi(\Sigma_\gamma) \cdot \mathrm{const}, where \Sigma_\gamma is any Seifert surface spanning \gamma.

Scope. The classical identity \lim_{q \to 1} E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho) = E(\varrho)/4 + \text{const} is stated in the archimedean realisation K = \mathbb{R}; the right-hand side E(\varrho) is a Lebesgue integral on S^1 \times S^1. Under a surreal lift (see appendix on surreal lift), the left-hand side E_{\mathrm{cat}} lifts verbatim (categorical operations only) and \lim_{q \to 1} becomes \mathrm{st} \circ \text{eval}_{q = 1 + \varepsilon}; the right-hand side remains in \mathbb{R} as an external anchor. Lebesgue measure is not used inside QOU. \square
lem:jones-mobius-diagonal:
Lemma Jones polynomial as the diagonal of the categorical Möbius kernel. Let

  K_q(s,t) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Delta(\varrho(s)) \otimes \Delta(\varrho(t))\bigr)

be the categorical Möbius two-point kernel of prop:mobius-energy, which collapses to the repulsive 1/\lvert\varrho(s)-\varrho(t)\rvert^2 as q \to 1 (Frobenius–Hopf kernel). Write the Hadamard finite-part decomposition of the categorical Möbius energy obtained by excising the diagonal,

  E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{T_{\mathrm{reg}}(\varrho)}_{\text{regularized two-point}}
  \;-\;
  \underbrace{C(\varrho)}_{\text{diagonal contact}} ,

Then the contact coefficient C(\varrho) is the fundamental (N=2) Markov trace, whose braid closure is the Jones polynomial (Jones–Markov trace)

  C(\varrho) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_K)) \;=\; J_K(q).

Consequently

  J_K(q) \;=\; T_{\mathrm{reg}}(\varrho) \;-\; E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho):

The fundamental Jones polynomial is exactly the self-energy that the Möbius renormalization subtracts. The fundamental Jones data embeds into the Möbius two-point data as its contact / diagonal term; the converse map loses the off-diagonal fusion content \Delta(e_\lambda) = \sum_{\mu\nu} N^\lambda_{\mu\nu}\, e_\mu \otimes e_\nu.
prf:jones-mobius-diagonal:
Proof Proof of jones mobius diagonal. The kernel collapse (Frobenius–Hopf kernel) gives K_q(s,t) \to 1/r^2 on the diagonal; its coincidence residue is the fundamental two-point contact C(\varrho), which by the Jones–Markov identity (Jones–Markov trace) is the single-element Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_K)) = J_K(q). The categorical Möbius energy is, by definition, the regularized two-point integral with this contact removed — the O'Hara / Freedman–He–Wang Hadamard finite part. Rearranging the renormalization identity E_{\mathrm{cat}} = T_{\mathrm{reg}} - C gives C = T_{\mathrm{reg}} - E_{\mathrm{cat}}, that is J_K = T_{\mathrm{reg}} - E_{\mathrm{cat}}. The off-diagonal remainder retains the comultiplication's fusion coefficients N^\lambda_{\mu\nu}, which the single-element trace does not resolve; hence the embedding is strict. \qquad\blacksquare

Scope. This is the fundamental (N=2) base of the embedding. The N-coloured contacts form the coloured-Markov-trace family \mathrm{tr}_M^{(N)}(\rho(\beta_K)); the present lemma is the N=2 rung on which that tower is built, not a claim about the limit.
cor:non-self-intersection:
Corollary Obstruction to self-intersection. Let \varrho be a knot embedding with categorical Möbius energy E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho) as in Proposition, and let q \neq 1 be the substrate parameter (Definition).

The non-cocommutativity of the Hopf structure at q \neq 1 provides a categorical obstruction to self-intersection:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \longrightarrow \infty
  \quad\text{as two non-adjacent strands of } \varrho \text{ approach within the fibre } \tau(A).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
lem:nsi-q-deformed-kernel:
Lemma q-deformed commutator replaces 1/r^2 with a hard kernel at r = \hbar_q. For q \neq 1, the categorical mass of a vortex filament \varrho inherits a kernel

  \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
   \longmapsto 
  \frac{[2]_q}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2
  - \hbar_q^{2}},

where [2]_q = q + q^{-1} and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}. The kernel possesses a hard singularity at \lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q.
prf:nsi-q-deformed-kernel:
Proof Proof that the q-deformed kernel has a hard singularity at \hbar_q. For q \neq 1, the braiding \check{R} = \sigma \circ \mathcal{R} is non-trivial, and the categorical mass acquires a singular contribution from non-adjacent strand proximity. Concretely, because \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) depends on the q-Hodge star \star_q (Definition), the cost of two non-adjacent points \varrho(s), \varrho(t) approaching is governed by the q-deformed commutator

  [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q
  = 
  \hat{X}\hat{P} - q\hat{P}\hat{X}
  = 
  i\hbar_q,

which replaces the classical 1/r^2 repulsion kernel with the strictly stronger

  \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
   \longmapsto 
  \frac{[2]_q}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2
  - \hbar_q^{2}},

where [2]_q = q + q^{-1} is the quantum integer and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant. This kernel has a hard singularity at \lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q, creating an energy barrier of infinite height at the quantum scale. \square
prf:non-self-intersection:
Proof Proof of Obstruction to self-intersection. The mechanism is as follows. The universal R-matrix \mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) (Remark) controls the failure of the cocommutativity square

  \sigma \circ \Delta  \neq  \Delta,

where \sigma is the tensor swap. At q = 1 one has \mathcal{R} = 1 \otimes 1 and the comultiplication is cocommutative, so strands may pass through each other freely (the "classical" regime where self-intersection is not penalised by the energy functional).

For q \neq 1, by (q-deformed kernel with hard singularity), the classical 1/r^2 repulsion kernel is replaced by [2]_q / (\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2 - \hbar_q^2), which has a hard singularity at \lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q, creating an energy barrier of infinite height at the quantum scale. \square
rem:non-self-intersection-interpretation: Remark Quantum exclusion zone and the Pauli analogue. Physically, the R-matrix endows the vortex filament \varrho with a "quantum exclusion zone" of radius \hbar_q. The filament cannot pass through itself because doing so would demand infinite categorical energy. This constitutes the knot-theoretic analogue of the Pauli exclusion principle, with the non-cocommutativity of \Delta_q serving as fermionic statistics.
sec:crossing-energy-intro: Localizing the global Möbius self-avoidance kernel at the crossings of a braid projection decomposes the crossing energy E_\times (Definition) into a symmetric strong baseline and an orientation-odd electromagnetic shift proportional to the Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{H}) = \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) (Definition). This section develops these crossing-energy identities on the trefoil and in the commutative limit over the categorical coordinate ring R[i, q^{\pm 1}].
rem:crossing-energy-categorical-origin:
Remark Crossing weights are Hecke eigenvalues, not postulates. The per-crossing weights (q, -q^{-1}) of the crossing energy are not an energetic penalty laid on top of a topological framework. They are the two eigenvalues of the Hecke generator T = P \circ R \colon V \otimes V \to V \otimes V acting on the symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition. The rigid monoidal structure forces them:

  1. Rigidity fixes the R-matrix determinant. Dualisability of V and the categorical volume constraint (volume constraint) require the braiding R = c_{V,V} to satisfy \det(R|_{V \otimes V}) = 1, with eigenvalues (q, q^{-1}) on S^{2} V \oplus \Lambda^{2} V.
  2. The Hecke generator carries the transposition sign. The Hecke generator is T = P \circ R, where P is the swap. Since P|_{\Lambda^{2} V} = -\mathrm{id}, composition flips the sign on the antisymmetric summand. This gives T-eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) with \det(T) = -1, which matches the Hecke minimal polynomial (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 (eigenvalue extraction).
  3. Crossing weights are eigenvalues, not postulates. Assigning a positive crossing L_{+} the weight q and a negative crossing L_{-} the weight -q^{-1} represents precisely the action of T on a symmetric-channel input and T^{-1} on an antisymmetric-channel input. The sum \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) is therefore a trace of T^{\pm 1}-eigenvalues along the braid. The categorical structure dictates this assignment.
  4. Gröbner--Shirshov resolution. When \mathfrak{H} is reduced to Gröbner--Shirshov normal form, each crossing contributes its T-eigenvalue exactly once. The net \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} is the resulting Laurent polynomial in q, read off the normal form. Removing any of these weights would violate duality and break the Hecke relation.

Compute this quantity entirely from the R-matrix braiding (R-matrix) of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) acting on the tensor product of constituent representations.
ex:crossing-energy-trefoil:
Example Crossing energy and binding in the trefoil. Evaluate the crossing energy (crossing energy) for the trefoil knot and then detail how binding arises in hadrons.

Single crossing energy. Each crossing in a knot diagram carries Skein weight q (positive crossing) or -q^{-1} (negative crossing). For a positive crossing, the energy contribution is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}^{(+)} = q,
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}^{(-)} = -q^{-1}.

The net energy of a single positive crossing minus a single negative crossing is q - q^{-1}. This coefficient appears in the Skein relation T - T^{-1} = q - q^{-1}.

Trefoil: three positive crossings. The standard diagram of the trefoil \tau(2,3) has three positive crossings. Its total crossing energy is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\tau(2,3))
  =  3q.

At the substrate parameter q \approx 1.110:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\tau(2,3))
   \approx  3 \times 1.110
  =  3.330.

This is positive. The trefoil is a single knot, not a composite, so there is no linking to provide negative binding energy.

Binding in composites. A hadron \mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} is a composite. Its linking \mathcal{L} introduces additional crossings between constituent knots. Mutual crossings between distinct components can contribute negative energy (via negative crossings in the linking braid word). The total crossing energy of a composite is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H})
  = 
  \underbrace{\sum_{i} \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K_i)}_{\text{self-crossings (positive)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{L})}_{\text{mutual crossings (can be negative)}}.

The composite is bound when the total is negative: \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) < 0. The mutual linking energy overcomes the individual knot crossing costs. The composite is energetically favorable relative to the separated constituents.

Proton binding. The proton (proton as Borromean hadron) consists of three quarks linked in a Borromean configuration. The Borromean linking contributes enough negative mutual crossing energy to make \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. This explains why the proton is a stable bound state: disassembling it into free quarks demands adding energy equal to |\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p})|.
rem:commutative-crossing-energy:
Remark Categorical coordinate of the commutative limit: i as \sqrt{\lambda_-} and the \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}(1) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}_q(1) hierarchy. The Hecke generator \sigma = P \circ R on V \otimes V has eigenvalues (\lambda_+, \lambda_-) = (q, -q^{-1}) on the symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V (def:crossing-energy). At q = 1 (def:commutative-qou), the eigenvalues collapse to (+1, -1) = \mathbb{Z}_2, and the per-crossing weight q - q^{-1} vanishes identically. The categorical structure of the commutative limit is recovered by extracting the square root of the antisymmetric eigenvalue \lambda_- = -1:

  i  =  \sqrt{\lambda_-}, \qquad i^2 + 1  =  0  \;\text{in}\; R[i].

The categorical structure forces the ring extension R[i] (the universal R-algebra containing an element i with i^2 = -1). The element i is the categorical coordinate of \mathbb{P}(V) in the commutative limit, mirroring the role of q in the non-commutative theory. The construction is intrinsic to R; no real or complex numbers are assumed. When R already contains a square root of -1 (e.g. the archimedean realisation where R = \mathbb{C}, see archimedean realisations), i \in R is canonical. When R does not (e.g. R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] at q = 1), R[i] is the minimal extension realising \lambda_- as a categorical square.

Categorical-coordinate dictionary.

See Table 1.

Deformation hierarchy. The discrete Weyl group \mathbb{Z}_2 embeds into the continuous maximal torus, which itself is the q = 1 fibre of the quantum torus:

  \mathbb{Z}_2  \;\hookrightarrow\;  \mathrm{U}(1)  \;\hookrightarrow\;
   \mathrm{U}_q(1).

Each inclusion identifies a different categorical coordinate on \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}). The value -1 generates \mathbb{Z}_2; i generates \mathrm{U}(1) at the quarter-turn \varTheta = \pi/2; and q generates \mathrm{U}_q(1) off-locus. The standard non-commutative deformation \mathrm{SU}(2) \rightsquigarrow \mathrm{SU}_q(2) acts on the second inclusion. The commutative-limit enlargement \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}(1) acts on the first. These are the two mechanisms to escape the q = 1 degeneracy of q - q^{-1}.

Three categorical readings of i on \mathbb{P}(V).

  1. Algebraic. i = \sqrt{\lambda_-} \in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(\mathbf{1}) is the categorical square root of the antisymmetric braiding eigenvalue. This single datum appears in three faces: Wick rotation, CR complex structure, and arrow of time. All reduce to the binary choice of braiding orientation c_{V,V} vs c_{V,V}^{-1} (rem:i-as-braiding-orientation).
  2. Geometric. J = i \cdot \mathrm{id}_V \in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(V) is an endomorphism with J^2 = -\mathrm{id}_V, descending to a complex structure on \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathrm{Proj}(\mathrm{Sym}\, V^\vee) over R[i]. In the archimedean realisation, this recovers the standard complex structure on the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2 (def:exceptional-divisor).
  3. Equivariant. The maximal torus \mathrm{U}(1) \subset \mathrm{SU}(2) acts on \mathbb{P}(V) with i as the quarter-turn generator. The orbit space is [0, \pi] with phase fibre \varphi \in S^1 over the interior (prop:u1-equivariant-reduction).

The three readings coincide because each computes the same categorical datum: a square root of \lambda_- in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(V).

Affine-chart origin. Both q and i originate from the chart-transition data of \mathbb{P}(V) (rem:affine-chart-origin-of-i-and-q). The parameter q constitutes the chart-transition coefficient z\,w = q^{-1} on the quantum projective line \mathbb{P}_q(V). The element i is the square root of the chart-swap involution \iota: z \mapsto z^{-1} that the transition collapses to at q = 1. Formally, the categorical-coordinate ring is the universal R-algebra extension R[i, q^{\pm 1}] = R[q, q^{-1}][i]/(i^2 + 1) (prop:categorical-coordinate-ring) in which q is invertible and the involution-eigenvalue -1 possesses a square root. The chart-transition automorphism group factors as \langle q \rangle \rtimes \langle \iota \rangle over this ring.

Half-twist and ribbon structures. The ribbon element v = q^{1/2} is not required for the categorical-coordinate construction. It appears only when \mathbf{C} carries an additional ribbon twist \varTheta_V = q^{1/2}\,\mathrm{id}_V for framed-link invariants or Reshetikhin--Turaev TQFT (rem:sqrt-q-ribbon-structure). Extract the square root of \lambda_- within R[i], not from any ribbon datum. It remains independent of the eigenvalue-labelling convention q := \lambda_+ (rem:braiding-unit-circle-convention).

Crossing energy in the commutative limit. Setting q = e^{i\varTheta} on the unit circle of \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) gives

  q - q^{-1}  =  2i \sin\varTheta,

with \varTheta \in [0, \pi] tracking the orbit-space interval of prop:u1-equivariant-reduction. The endpoints \varTheta = 0, \pi define the polar fixed points (zero weight). The interior constitutes the free S^1-fibre. The point \varTheta = \pi/2 (where q = i) marks the location of maximum weight |2i \sin(\pi/2)| = 2. The Hecke energy q - q^{-1} of the non-commutative theory operates as the algebraic deformation of this commutative-limit form.
